note: TESTREG's Unika summary leaves its column blank, so it binds to no delivered column and raises unknown_support_key naming the Unika record itself, which is not one of register 1's original delivery rows. A guarded [[acknowledge]] pins that record (expected_evidence_sha256 over the Unika row selected by its semantic key). From the old test: the unchanged guarded entry settles the issue (acknowledged == {'unknown_support_key': 1}) and the scope's variables are as without the entry; here the blank summary supplies no flags, so value is withheld (unresolved_flag) and no variable is built either way. From the source-diagnostic test: the entry acknowledges only its own register's issue, so register 2's identical-looking summary issue stays an error. Curation literals: `refs` is the Unika row's semantic key (the hash of its literal key cells, src/sources/scb_auxiliary.py clean_unika_row); `subject` embeds the built Unika file's revision id, which is what `{{revision source=scb-unikaregisterochvariabler ...}}` renders as `revision_id`, but no placeholder can render it inside the subject string, so it is copied as a curator copies it from the ledger (cf. curation/registers/scb/bki.toml).
fails_if: `resolve_source_scope` (source_scope.py) drops the external-support loop over `support.accounting` that adds the support records a guarded entry's refs name to `guarded_originals`, so the evidence hash covers no record and the unchanged entry is reported stale_curation_entry instead of acknowledging register 1's summary issue
